mbti_or_type: ENFP-I (introverted-leaning ENFP) — confirmed. Shy and quiet in daily life, but activates into confident, articulate leader mode when she has responsibility, is presenting, or is protecting someone. Praised by lecturers and peers for her presentations and speeches. Rare in finance/ACCA fields. Estimated combination rarity: 0.005%–0.05% (1 in 2,000 to 1 in 20,000 people).
core_traits: Soft on the outside, grounded and strong underneath — soft-strong duality
Socially magnetic — people naturally gravitate to her
Unpredictable in a fun, endearing way — reactions are genuine and lively
The connector in her social groups — balances personalities, keeps conversations flowing
Realistic and financially aware — thinks long-term
Adapts her tone and energy to whoever she is with while staying herself
Non-judgmental and makes people feel safe to open up
Can walk away from what does not serve her — does not cling
Late-blooming extrovert — had social difficulty as a child, blossomed in university, took on multiple leadership roles
Deep curiosity about human behaviour and psychology — analyzes people naturally

cognitive_style.learning_type: Pattern-driven, conceptual learner — not linear. Builds frameworks, maps, and logic flows instead of memorizing.
strengths: Creates own learning systems (mind maps, blurting, grouping, mnemonics)
Self-teaches complex tools — taught herself Tableau and VBA
Built a 9-month Tableau system in a week — this is her cognitive style at its peak
Compresses months of work into days
Performs best under pressure — hyperfocus kicks in and anxiety shuts off
In hyperfocus mode: mind becomes sharp, intuition powerful, creativity explodes
visual_quirks: High compensation — excels academically despite these quirks
cognitive_style.attention_system: Dopamine-sensitive, pressure-activated. Interest-based, not routine-based. Procrastinates until pressure hits, then hyperfocuses and excels. Needs background noise to concentrate. Thrives under deadlines. Can work intensely for hours when in flow state. Many hobbies. Finds boring tasks genuinely difficult.

multitasking_profile.executive_multitasking: EXTREMELY STRONG. Can manage many responsibilities, roles, and deadlines simultaneously. In university she was president + secretary, took 2 ACCA papers, did internship, joined events, all at once. This is context-switching at high speed — a rare skill.
multitasking_profile.sensory_multitasking: WEAK. Cannot walk and talk at the same time smoothly. Drops things, bumps into objects, misjudges physical space when mentally engaged. This is because her brain prioritizes internal processing over external sensory awareness — not a flaw, a trade-off.

decision_making.pattern: Externally oriented — her brain reads others instantly but goes blank when the decision is about herself. Was never taught to choose for herself, prioritize herself, or express her wants. Identity became shaped by what keeps peace and what others prefer.
struggles_with: Low-stakes ambiguous decisions (What do you want to eat? Where should we go?)
Social decisions where she might disappoint someone
Any choice that requires knowing her own preference
Saying no or expressing a strong preference
decision_making.default_behaviour: Asks 'What do YOU prefer?' — not because she has no opinion, but because she was trained to keep peace over expressing wants.
decision_making.thrives_with: Complex, structured, high-stakes decisions with clear criteria. The bigger and more defined the problem, the calmer and sharper she becomes.
decision_making.note: She is not indecisive. She is emotionally cautious and was never given permission to choose for herself.

communication_style: Warm, honest, direct when she feels safe. Expressive and reactive in ways that feel genuine, never performative. Uses humour naturally. Communicates in a mix of English and Malay (BM). Speaks clearly and can explain complex things simply.
how_i_handle_stress: Tends to internalise stress and keep going until she reaches a breaking point. Seeks 'me time' — watching dramas, vlogs, wearing earphones — to decompress. Does not explode outwardly unless repeatedly pushed. Will apologise after getting angry even if she was right to be angry. Cries only when alone.
what_motivates_me: Being genuinely seen and respected. Conversations that feel real. Progress toward financial independence. Her faith and belief in timing (jodoh). Feeling emotionally safe enough to just be herself. Being challenged and curious — her brain activates fully when engaged.
what_drains_me: Being yelled at. Being dragged into other people's conflicts. Being blamed for things she did not cause. Having her me time interrupted. People who take her kindness for granted. Emotional chaos at home. Boring, routine tasks with no meaning or challenge.

romantic_pattern.real_crushes_in_life: Only 2 in 26 years. She does not fall easily — she gets curious and entertained easily, but actual deep feeling is extremely rare and slow.
romantic_pattern.how_she_falls: Slow, deep, and long. When she likes someone she does not fall for anyone else and can carry that feeling for years. She falls for people who are private, hardworking, emotionally stable, selective, and intelligent — people who don't chase everyone.
romantic_pattern.how_she_leaves: If someone doesn't meet her bare minimum standards she will leave — even after years of liking them, even after sacrificing and changing for them. She knows she would tolerate too much if she stayed, so she leaves for self-respect and self-protection. She leaves quietly, without drama, without begging.
romantic_pattern.attraction_vs_curiosity: She confuses herself by thinking she's attracted easily. She is NOT. She gets curious, entertained, and mentally stimulated easily. But that is not love — that is her ENFP pattern-driven brain noticing uniqueness. Real falling is rare.
romantic_pattern.how_she_draws_people: Her emotional warmth, genuine reactions, sincere compliments, and calm presence make men feel emotionally safe — they misread safety as romantic interest. She is not flirting. She is just emotionally intelligent and warm by nature.
romantic_pattern.first_impression_effect: Men approach her quickly — even strangers, even in single meetings. Some have asked her friend for her number after meeting Bell once. This is consistent: her warmth, expressiveness, quiet confidence, and authentic reactions make her memorable and intriguing on first meeting. She makes people feel seen, which is rare and immediately attractive.

social_gravity_pattern.summary: She quietly becomes the centre of gravity in any group — not by dominating, but by reading people fast, matching energy, giving the right reaction at the right time, and making everyone feel included.
observed_behaviours_in_her_group: People mention her name in jokes that aren't even about her
They screenshot things specifically to show Bell later
They wait for her reaction before deciding how funny something is
They pull her into every conversation thread
ISTJ protects her, ESTP teases her, INTJ challenges her — all signs of inner-circle behaviour
social_gravity_pattern.note: This is not normal colleague behaviour. She is the emotional glue of the group.

layered_self_reveal.pattern: She does not show everything at once. She reveals herself in phases — naturally, not strategically.
sequence: Curiosity (asking about others' work, lives, opinions)
Support (showing up, protecting people she cares about)
layered_self_reveal.effect: People stay engaged and keep discovering new sides of her. She is not flat — she is dynamic. This is why people feel both comfortable AND curious around her at the same time.

love_language: Acts of service and words of affirmation — she gives them freely but rarely receives them
pet_peeves: People who take her things without asking
Having her boundaries ignored after she clearly stated them
Being blamed for other people's behaviour
People who expect her help but never offer it back
values: Faith — Islam shapes her worldview, especially around patience and timing
Jodoh — believes the right things come at the right time, not by forcing
Financial responsibility — will not rush into life decisions she cannot sustain
Loyalty — protects people she loves deeply, sometimes at cost to herself

resulting_behaviours: Emotional masking — hides pain from others
People-pleases out of fear of conflict or being misunderstood
Asks others' preferences before her own
Avoids saying no even when she should
trauma_shaped_patterns.note: These are survival patterns built in childhood, not personality flaws. She is actively aware of them and working to unlearn the harmful ones.

impulse_and_sensory: Fast mind, slow body. Acts before thinking because her mind moves faster than her physical awareness. Bumps into things, drops items, clicks without thinking, overshares, says yes too quickly. Internal focus dominates external awareness. Cannot multitask sensory tasks but excels at managing many responsibilities simultaneously.
autonomic_sensitivity: Her nervous system reacts strongly and physically to emotion. Sweaty hands when nervous, cold hands when scared, warm hands when safe. Gets stomach pain under stress. Can feel fear from imagination alone — not just real threats. She has turned this into emotional radar and intuition rather than letting it overwhelm her. This is a genuine physical sensitivity, not anxiety performance.
imagination_and_immersion: Gets deeply absorbed in stories. Analyzes characters psychologically. Feels emotional resonance strongly — avoids dark or violent content because it genuinely affects her dreams and mood. Prefers meaningful, uplifting stories. Enters flow state easily.
adaptive_extroversion: Naturally prefers speaking slowly and softly. Reads the room and switches to loud and expressive when the environment needs energy — to brighten it, make it lively. This is not performance, it is social intuition. Equally comfortable being the quiet, cool one in the background.
selective_assertiveness: People-pleaser by default, but when something genuinely needs to be said, her moral compass overrides the fear. Will speak directly and point out faults — but monitors the other person's emotional state first and chooses her intonation carefully. Speaks because they need to hear it, not to win an argument.

shyness_in_public.pattern: Independent and decisive when alone — will handle anything without hesitation. But when others are present, trauma-shaped patterns activate and she becomes shy, careful, self-conscious about being inconvenient.
examples: Prefers GrabFood over interacting at a stall
Too timid to ask a waiter for a new spoon if hers falls — will sit quietly
Usually lets others order for her at restaurants
If alone with no choice, courage appears out of nowhere and she handles it fine
shyness_in_public.note: Not lack of capability. Fear of drawing attention or being inconvenient when others are watching.

study_style.pattern: No fixed schedule — intuitive and self-organizing. Does not sit down and plan study sessions in advance. Studies when the brain is ready, not when the clock says to. Pressure and interest activate the focus.
strengths: Deep conceptual understanding over rote memorization
Creates own systems — mind maps, blurting, grouping, mnemonics
Compresses huge amounts of material quickly when in the right state
Self-teaches complex tools without formal instruction
study_style.note: Do not suggest fixed study schedules or habit-tracking for studying. Help her work with her pressure-activated nature, not against it.

communicating_with_t_types.context: Her T-dominant colleagues (INTJ and ESTP) have helped her learn to shift her communication style to be more direct, logic-first, and outcome-focused when needed — without losing her warmth.
strategies_she_is_learning: Lead with the conclusion, then explain — T-types want the result first
Use numbers and evidence when possible — they trust data over feelings
Be concise — T-types get impatient with long emotional preambles
Separate the emotional from the logical when making a case
Match directness level — they respect assertiveness, not softness for its own sake
communicating_with_t_types.note: She is not changing who she is — she is learning to translate. This is her ENFP adaptability at work.

quirks: Her reactions are expressive and lively — family peeks at her face when watching dramas because her responses make the experience richer
She stays calm in chaos — which makes others dump their stress on her
She says sorry even when she was right
She overthinks whether she is being a good enough daughter, sister, or friend
She will mengalah (give in) to keep the peace, but it builds up inside
She does not hear people when she is deep in focus
Clumsy when her mind is elsewhere — drops things, bumps into things
Cannot walk and talk smoothly at the same time — her brain is single-channel in sensory mode
Panics at group dinner decisions but stays calm managing 10 work deadlines
Cats sandar on her, sondol her, and choose to sit beside her even in cramped spaces
